title: Content Delivery Network
summary: A CDN puts copies of your content in hundreds of data centres close to users, so most requests never travel to your servers. DNS or anycast steers each user to a nearby edge. The edge serves from cache when it can, and on a miss it asks a regional shield tier, so the origin sees one request instead of thousands.

walkthrough.title: Find the nearest edge
walkthrough.text: The browser resolves cdn.example.com. Anycast (one IP announced from every location) or a geo-aware DNS answer sends the user to a nearby point of presence (PoP).

walkthrough.title: Terminate TLS at the edge
walkthrough.text: The edge completes the TLS handshake a few milliseconds away instead of across an ocean, then builds a cache key from host, path, and selected headers or query params.

walkthrough.title: Cache miss goes to the shield
walkthrough.text: If the edge does not have the object, it asks a regional shield PoP instead of the origin. Many edges share one shield, which raises the hit ratio.

walkthrough.title: Shield fetches from origin
walkthrough.text: Only on a shield miss does the request reach the origin. Concurrent misses for the same object are coalesced into one origin fetch.

walkthrough.title: Push config and purges
walkthrough.text: Customers change rules or purge content through the control plane. Changes reach every PoP worldwide in seconds.

walkthrough.title: Serve and cache the response
walkthrough.text: The edge stores the object for its TTL (from Cache-Control) and returns it. With stale-while-revalidate, users get the old copy instantly while the edge refreshes it in the background.

data.label: User / Browser
responsibilities: Resolves the CDN hostname and connects to whichever IP DNS returns.
Reuses its own cache and revalidates with ETags so unchanged files cost a tiny 304.
Benefits from HTTP/3 (QUIC), which avoids head-of-line blocking on lossy mobile networks.

failureModes.scenario: Long-cached file changed without a new URL
failureModes.impact: Users keep seeing the old CSS or JS for days.
failureModes.mitigation: Fingerprinted file names (app.3f9a.js) with a long max-age; short TTL on HTML.
Anycast routing, or EDNS Client Subnet so DNS sees the user's real location.

data.label: DNS / Anycast Routing

output.name: Answer
output.type: IP of the best PoP (TTL 30-300 s)

responsibilities: Steers each user to a healthy PoP that is close in network terms.
Takes overloaded or failed PoPs out of rotation within seconds.
Absorbs DDoS traffic by spreading it across every anycast location.

failureModes.impact: Traffic lands in the wrong region or is black-holed.
failureModes.mitigation: RPKI route validation, staged route changes, and monitoring from many vantage points.

failureModes.scenario: PoP fails but DNS answers are cached
failureModes.impact: Users keep connecting to a dead PoP until the TTL expires.
failureModes.mitigation: Anycast withdraws the route instantly; short TTLs for DNS-based steering.

data.label: Control Plane

input.name: Change
input.type: Purge /products/*, or rule: cache /api/* for 10 s

output.name: Rollout
output.type: Versioned config + purge events pushed to every PoP

responsibilities: Stores customer config: cache rules, TLS certificates, WAF rules, edge functions.
Pushes purges worldwide in seconds, by URL, prefix, or surrogate-key tag.
Rolls out config gradually so a bad rule cannot take down every PoP at once.

failureModes.impact: Every PoP breaks at the same moment, a global outage.
failureModes.mitigation: Canary PoPs first, automatic rollback on error spikes, kill switch for edge code.

failureModes.impact: Everything is evicted and the origin is flooded with misses.
failureModes.mitigation: Prefer tag-based purges; soft purge (mark stale) so stale-while-revalidate still works.

data.label: Edge PoP Cache

input.name: Request
input.type: HTTPS GET + cache key (host + path + vary headers)

responsibilities: Terminates TLS close to the user and serves cached objects in a few milliseconds.
Builds cache keys carefully: varying on too many headers splits the cache into useless fragments.
Runs WAF rules, redirects, and small edge functions before anything reaches the origin.

failureModes.scenario: Cache key includes a random query param (utm_*, session id)
failureModes.impact: Every request is a miss; hit ratio collapses.
failureModes.mitigation: Normalise and strip unneeded params; allowlist the headers used for Vary.

failureModes.scenario: Personalised page cached and served to others
failureModes.impact: One user's account page shown to strangers, a data leak.
failureModes.mitigation: Cache-Control: private on personalised responses; never cache responses with Set-Cookie.

data.label: Origin Shield

input.name: Edge misses
input.type: GETs from many PoPs in the region

output.name: Origin fetch
output.type: One GET per object per TTL

responsibilities: Acts as a large shared cache between the edges and the origin.
Coalesces concurrent misses for the same object into a single origin request.
Serves stale content if the origin is down (stale-if-error).

failureModes.impact: All edges in the region send misses straight to the origin.
failureModes.mitigation: Fail over to a secondary shield; rate-limit origin fetches.

failureModes.scenario: Thundering herd when a hot object expires
failureModes.mitigation: Request coalescing, plus refreshing just before expiry.

data.label: Origin Server
responsibilities: Holds the source of truth for every file and page.
Decides cacheability with Cache-Control, Surrogate-Control, and Vary headers.
Accepts traffic only from the CDN so attackers cannot bypass it.

failureModes.impact: Uncached and expired content fails to load.
failureModes.mitigation: stale-if-error serves the last good copy; multi-region origin.

failureModes.impact: Attackers hit it directly, bypassing CDN DDoS protection.
failureModes.mitigation: Firewall to CDN IP ranges only, or a private tunnel or mTLS from the CDN.
